intro: Sai Aarogya Hospital in Bapatla operates under the auspices of the Sri Madhusudan Sai Global Humanitarian Mission, reflecting its unwavering commitment to delivering high-quality secondary care to underserved rural communities across India. With the 30-50 bedded facilities strategically established in Bapatla, Andhra Pradesh, the hospital bridges the healthcare gap for rural populations while complementing the primary care services provided by our Sai Swasthya Wellness Centres.

Rooted in the Mission's guiding principle of selfless service, all services are offered completely free of charge to every individual, without discrimination based on caste, creed, religion, or economic status. By ensuring equitable access to quality healthcare, Sai Aarogya Hospital is advancing the Mission's vision of creating a healthier and more inclusive society.

inspiration.name: Sri Sathya Sai Baba
body: Sri Sathya Sai Baba was a revered spiritual leader and philanthropist, known for his teachings on universal love, service, and the unity of all religions. His philosophy emphasised the principles of love, peace, truth, right conduct, and non-violence, encapsulated in the phrase “Love All, Serve All.”

He established numerous educational institutions, hospitals, and social welfare projects, providing free education, healthcare, and drinking water to millions. Driven by the belief that service to humanity is service to God, we have been striving to engage in selfless service to uplift the needy. The Sai Aarogya initiative continues this legacy by delivering free, compassionate, and comprehensive healthcare services to those in need.

founder.name: Sri Madhusudan Sai
founder.quote: Vasudhaiva kutumbakam – One World One Family
body: Sri Madhusudan Sai is a humanitarian leader whose mission of service and spirituality extends across the globe. Since 2012, he has dedicated his life to uplifting millions through free nutrition, education, and healthcare initiatives. Guided by the ancient Indian principle of vasudhaiva kutumbakam - One World One Family, Sri Madhusudan Sai envisions a world where nations, societies, and individuals support one another as a family.

Through his tireless efforts and inspiring leadership, he has created a model of selfless service that transcends borders, touching countless lives with care and compassion, all provided free of charge and without discrimination.

mission.name: Sri Madhusudan Sai Global Humanitarian Mission
body: The Sri Madhusudan Sai Global Humanitarian Mission has a unique global vision that harmoniously fuses service and spirituality, extending its impact across the world. Since its inception in 2012 under the guidance of its Founder, Sri Madhusudan Sai, the Mission has established Institutes of Excellence in four key areas: nutrition, education, healthcare, and spirituality. Sai Aarogya is one such initiative under the Mission, providing free and accessible healthcare to underserved communities.

The Mission's unwavering commitment to service and spirituality has made a profound impact on communities worldwide. By nurturing young minds, empowering individuals through education, and providing free healthcare services, the Mission is actively working towards a world where everyone has the opportunity to thrive and live a life of dignity and purpose.

trust.name: Sri Sathya Sai Sujala Sravanthi Trust
body: The Sri Sathya Sai Sujala Sravanthi Trust, established in 2012, is one of the trusts supporting the Sri Madhusudan Sai Global Humanitarian Mission. Dedicated to uplifting underserved communities, the Trust drives a wide range of charitable initiatives aligned with the Mission's vision of selfless service.

The Trust focuses on providing essential support in critical areas such as drinking water, sanitation, rural infrastructure, education, nutrition, and healthcare. Operating entirely on a voluntary basis, the Trust embodies the Mission's ethos of selfless service, creating lasting positive change and improving the well-being of communities.

history: The healthcare journey at Kajipalem Village, Bapatla District, began with a 20-bed hospital operated by a group of NRI philanthropists under the name Aravinda Ashramam. Despite its early success, the hospital encountered challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic, including a shortage of doctors and resources, which led to a decline in healthcare services.

In August 2023, the Aravinda Ashramam team approached the Sri Sathya Sai Sujala Sravanthi Trust for collaboration to rejuvenate healthcare in the region. This partnership, under the aegis of the Sri Madhusudan Sai Global Humanitarian Mission, established a Sai Swasthya Wellness Centre in October 2023 to provide immediate healthcare support.

The Sai Aarogya Hospital in Bapatla represents a significant expansion of this effort, with preparations for the new facility commencing in January 2024. Inaugurated on December 13, 2024, the hospital will operate in collaboration with the Sri Madhusudan Sai Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (SMSIMSR) and the Sanjeevani Hospitals, a chain of paediatric cardiac hospitals that are also part of the Mission. This collaborative approach exemplifies the Mission’s holistic vision of providing free, high-quality healthcare to underserved communities, ensuring well-being for all.

people.name: R Venkateswara Rao
people.bio: An M.Tech graduate in Civil Engineering, R. Venkateswara Rao retired as Engineer-in-Chief from the Panchayat Raj Engineering Department after 39 years of service. Currently, he serves as a Technical Advisor to APMSIDC, contributing to hospital infrastructure development and overseeing the construction of 16 medical colleges under the Nadu-Nedu program.

people.name: R Kondala Rao
people.bio: Retired Engineer-in-Chief of the Panchayat Raj and Rural Water Supply Departments, R. Kondala Rao played a pivotal role in Sri Sathya Sai Water Supply Projects. He continues to serve as a Technical Advisor to the Government of Andhra Pradesh, contributing to public service and rural infrastructure development.

people.name: Veeramachaneni Sivaprasad
people.bio: As the proprietor of Saiteja Constructions, Veeramachaneni Sivaprasad has delivered large-scale construction projects while also engaging deeply in philanthropic efforts, including building free schools and hostels for underserved communities.

people.name: Kalyan Chakravarthy Konduri
people.bio: With over 20 years of experience in the BFSI sector, Kalyan is a Trustee and Secretary of the Trust. A long-time associate of Sri Sathya Sai’s mission, he has actively contributed to projects in rural infrastructure, healthcare, and education.

people.name: G Dharma Data
people.bio: A retired Director of Drugs Control Administration, Andhra Pradesh, G Dharma Data is an esteemed pharmaceutical leader and academic. He continues to impact the field as an Adjunct Professor, Regulatory Advisor, and President of the Indian Pharmacy Graduates Association.

people.name: DVN Raju
people.bio: Whole-time Director of Island Veerchemie, a pioneer in manufacturing Sodium Azide, and an active philanthropist.

people.name: Nagaraju Penumetsa
people.bio: An entrepreneur with over 32 years of global corporate experience, Nagaraju brings his vision to initiatives like the Suryalanka Shivakshetram Temple project.

people.name: Karuna Raju Manthena
people.bio: With 25 years of association with Sri Sathya Sai’s mission, Karuna Raju leverages his expertise in construction, hospital management, and strategic planning.

people.name: R Lakshmipathi
people.bio: Former Chairman of APMSIDC, R Lakshmipathi has a distinguished career in infrastructure and community development.
